question: Which statement correctly reflects the weighted voting system under Article 279A(9)?

options.text: Centre plus one state can pass decisions
States have double the Centre’s voting weight
Centre and States have equal votes

solution:
The correct answer is __**Centre holds 75 percent voting share**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 279A(9)** of the Constitution of India governs the decision-making process of the **Goods and Services Tax (GST) Council**. It specifies the weighted voting system for the council members.
 
• The voting weight is distributed between the **Centre** and the **States/Union Territories (UTs)**. The Centre holds a **75% voting share**, while the States/UTs collectively hold **25% voting share**.
 
• For a decision to pass, it requires a majority of **three-fourths (75%) of the weighted votes**. This ensures that both Centre and States play a role in decision-making.
 
• The Centre’s dominant share in voting ensures its ability to influence decisions, keeping in mind national priorities while balancing the federal structure of governance.
 
• The weighted voting system is designed to maintain **collaborative federalism**, ensuring that the States have a say while respecting the Centre’s overarching role in tax administration. *Hence, the statement "Centre holds 75 percent voting share" is correct.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **GST Council:**

 
 
• The GST Council was constituted as per **Article 279A** of the Indian Constitution to make recommendations on important matters related to **Goods and Services Tax (GST).**
 
• The Council is chaired by the **Union Finance Minister**, with State Finance Ministers or their representatives as members.
 
• It is responsible for decisions like tax rates, exemptions, and procedural rules under GST. 
 
 
 
• **Decision-making Process:**
 
 
• Decision-making within the GST Council follows a **weighted voting system**, ensuring the representation of both the Centre and States.
 
• The Centre’s voting weight is **75%**, while States/UTs share a collective **25%**.
 
• A **three-fourths majority** is required for a resolution to pass, promoting consensus and cooperation.
 
 
 
• **Federal Structure in GST:**
 
 
• The GST Council is an example of **cooperative federalism**, where the Centre and States collaborate to streamline taxation and revenue collection.
 
• The voting system ensures that while the Centre has a significant role, States/UTs also have a voice in the decision-making process.
 
• This balances national interests with regional concerns, fostering better governance. 
 
 
 
• **Important Features of GST:**
 
 
• GST is a **destination-based tax**, meaning taxes are collected at the point of consumption rather than origin.
 
• It subsumes multiple indirect taxes like excise duty, VAT, and service tax into one unified system.
 
• The implementation of GST aims to reduce **tax cascading** and improve tax compliance. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Statement Analysis:**

 
 
• Option 1: **"Centre holds 75 percent voting share"** – Correct, as per Article 279A(9).
 
• Option 2: **"Centre plus one state can pass decisions"** – Incorrect, as decisions require a three-fourths majority of weighted votes.
 
• Option 3: **"States have double the Centre’s voting weight"** – Incorrect, as States collectively hold only 25% of the weight.
 
• Option 4: **"Centre and States have equal votes"** – Incorrect, the Centre has a significantly higher voting share than States.
 
 
 
• **Evolution of GST:**
 
 
• GST was implemented in **India on 1st July 2017**, replacing multiple indirect taxes.
 
• It is guided by the GST Council, which ensures uniformity and resolves disputes regarding tax matters.
 
• The GST Act was passed in **2016**, making it one of the most significant tax reforms in India’s history.
